The main takeaway from our work is that

the growth-mortality rate trade-off is a fundamental aspect of the ecology of tree communities, which can be understood by combining information about the spatial variation in resource availability caused by canopy disturbance with information on inherent species differences in resource acquisition, dispersal ability, growth rate, and shade tolerance.
